en-el-hum1.title: Identidad Cultural y Lenguaje
en-el-hum1.concept: El lenguaje es más que una herramienta de comunicación; encarna la memoria colectiva y la visión del mundo.
en-el-hum1.example: Language is not merely a vehicle for exchanging factual information; it carries the collective memory and values of a community. When an endangered language disappears, humanity loses a unique lens through which the natural world was understood and classified.

en-el-hum2.title: Ética en el Mundo Moderno
en-el-hum2.concept: Analiza dilemas morales entre decisiones individuales y responsabilidad cívica en sociedades digitales.
en-el-hum2.example: Moral decisions in interconnected societies rarely affect only the decision-maker. As digital networks amplify individual actions, personal choices regarding data sharing and public discourse inevitably ripple across the entire social fabric, demanding a renewed sense of civic responsibility.

en-el-sci1.title: IA y la Mente Humana
en-el-sci1.concept: Examina el reconocimiento de patrones computacionales frente a la conciencia humana corporizada.
en-el-sci1.example: While generative models excel at predicting plausible token sequences based on vast corpora, they do not possess subjective experience or intentionality. Human comprehension is grounded in physical embodiment and emotional salience, aspects that purely statistical text processing cannot replicate.

en-el-sci2.title: Resiliencia Climática y Tecnologías Verdes
en-el-sci2.concept: Analiza marcos de economía circular y la desconexión energética de los combustibles fósiles.
en-el-sci2.example: Mitigating catastrophic climate risk requires more than incremental efficiency gains; it calls for a paradigm shift toward circular economic frameworks where materials are endlessly repurposed and energy grids decouple entirely from fossil fuels.

en-el-eco1.title: Economía Conductual y Toma de Decisiones
en-el-eco1.concept: Investiga la irracionalidad humana, la aversión a la pérdida y los marcos cognitivos en las decisiones.
en-el-eco1.example: Traditional neoclassical economic models presumed perfectly rational agents maximizing utility. However, empirical behavioral research demonstrates that humans exhibit profound loss aversion, weighing potential losses far more heavily than equivalent gains.

en-el-eco2.title: Globalización y Comercio Digital
en-el-eco2.concept: Explora los flujos de datos transfronterizos y la reorganización estructural de las cadenas de valor globales.
en-el-eco2.example: Modern globalization extends far beyond the physical transit of manufactured goods. Digital platforms have decoupled value creation from geographic proximity, allowing micro-enterprises to access worldwide capital markets while simultaneously introducing unprecedented regulatory challenges.

en-el-aca1.title: Premisas Lógicas y Supuestos Implícitos
en-el-aca1.concept: Identifica suposiciones no declaradas y evalúa la validez lógica de premisas y conclusiones.
en-el-aca1.example: Scientific progress does not advance solely through the steady accumulation of verified facts; rather, as foundational paradigms encounter persistent anomalies, scientific communities must undergo revolutionary conceptual reorganizations that redefine fundamental questions.

en-el-aca2.title: Síntesis Comparativa de Argumentos
en-el-aca2.concept: Sintetiza perspectivas divergentes y reconcilia argumentos complejos entre múltiples textos.
en-el-aca2.example: Passage A argues that technological automation invariably destroys employment faster than new industries can generate replacement roles. Passage B contends that historical transitions always yield higher-order cognitive vocations that cannot be anticipated during periods of disruption.
